title: Real ROI: Lessons from Enterprises that have already succeeded with LLMs at Scale: Raza Habib
talk_summary: Raza Habib of Humanloop distills patterns from enterprises getting real ROI from LLM apps: center domain experts over ML specialists, make evaluation the spec from day one, and invest in logging/replay tooling. Concrete cases (Ironclad's Rivet, Notion, Filevine, Duolingo) show debugging traces and decomposed binary evals are what unblock production agents.

takeaways.technique: Decompose subjective criteria into small binary checks instead of one god metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Break evaluation criteria into small independently-scorable binary questions rather than asking an LLM judge vague 'is this good' questions, then aggregate; keep a scorecard of trade-offs rather than a single number.
takeaways.evidence_quote: he was the one who said kind of you're seeking this single God metric you're probably taking taking the wrong path

takeaways.technique: LLM-as-judge only on narrow, specific questions
takeaways.what_they_do: Use LLM judges for specific verifiable questions (tone appropriate for a child, does text contain these five points) and avoid ambiguous holistic judgments which produce noisy data and ordering bias.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you ask the model is this a good piece of writing that's a very ambiguous subjective evaluation you're going to get very noisy data

takeaways.technique: Full trace logging with replay of any production run
takeaways.what_they_do: Capture inputs/outputs at every stage so any run can be found and re-run with modified prompts/tools/evaluators; Ironclad built this as a weekend project and it saved their agent effort.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it was only after they had that ability to debug these traces that they realized that actually they were able to get to Performance that now is in production
takeaways.numbers: ~50% of contracts auto-negotiated for biggest customers (post-tooling)

takeaways.technique: Evolve eval criteria during prototyping, then freeze as regression suite
takeaways.what_they_do: Ship a rough internal prototype fast, derive eval criteria from what 'good' looks like, distill into rigorous regression tests used before prompt/model changes and model migrations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you've built evaluation well from the start then a lot of these problems solve themselves

takeaways.technique: Domain experts own prompts, not just engineers
takeaways.what_they_do: Duolingo lets linguists write prompts and engineers don't edit them; Fathom has one PM own most summarization prompts because domain context determines what 'good' means.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they don't let the engineers of edit prompts that actually the linguists do all the prompt engineering

takeaways.technique: Keep pipelines simple; don't over-chain as models improve
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues most LLM apps are four simple blocks (model, prompt, data selection, tools) and that much chaining is a workaround for weak models that will shrink as models improve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keep things simple don't over complicate it um and just make these individual components good
